---
title: "Beans PCA: a recipe with no model"
---

The recipe is the product — extraction estimated on training data, judged on the validation set. No estimator anywhere. Ported from [Tidy Modeling with R, ch. 16](https://www.tmwr.org/dimensionality).

**Compare with R:** [side-by-side R ↔ Python](sbs/tmwr16-r-vs-py.html){target="_blank"} · R original: PC1–PC4 variance 59.4 / 24.4 / … (with orderNorm).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Port notes: gaps and parity vs the R original"}
```
The recipe IS the product: preprocessing estimated on training data, judged
visually on the validation set. No estimator anywhere.

PARITY NOTES:
 - GAP (blocking): step_pca -> StepPCA is designed-but-unbuilt (backlog
   priority 2). Stopgap: shoez does zv -> normalize, then sklearn's PCA
   consumes fitted.transform(validation) OUTSIDE the recipe. When StepPCA
   lands, the sklearn block collapses into .add(StepPCA(..., num_comp=4)).
 - GAP: step_orderNorm (bestNormalize's ORQ transform) has no shoez analog
   at all. Omitted: skewed shape features stay skewed; first run measured
   the effect — PC1-4 variance 55.4/26.5/8.0/5.1%.
 - R composes by piping MORE steps onto an already-prep()ed recipe and
   re-prepping; shoez has no incremental fit — declared whole, fit once.
 - beans exported from R on first run: data/beans.csv.
```
*Docs version loads vendored parquet from `examples/data/`; the research
originals export these datasets from R's modeldata at first run.*
:::

## Specify
```{python}
import polars as pl
from sklearn.decomposition import PCA
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from shoez import Recipe, StepDropZeroVariance, StepNormalize
from shoez import Selectors as s

# ── Data

beans = pl.read_parquet("data/beans.parquet")  # 13,611 x 17

# ── 3-way split (75 / 12.5 / 12.5, stratified by class)

bean_train, rest = train_test_split(
    beans, train_size=0.75, stratify=beans["class"],
    random_state=1601
)
bean_validation, bean_test = train_test_split(
    rest, train_size=0.50, stratify=rest["class"],
    random_state=1601
)

# ── Base recipe: zv -> (orderNorm GAP) -> normalize

bean_rec = (
    Recipe(data=bean_train, target="class")
    .add(StepDropZeroVariance(s.numeric_features()))
    # .add(StepOrderNorm(s.numeric_features()))   # 🧪 GAP: no analog at all
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_features()))
)
```
## Fit
```{python}
# fit() ~ prep(); transform() ~ bake() — the chapter doubles as the book's
# prep/bake tutorial, and this file doubles as shoez's fit/transform one.
fitted = bean_rec.fit(bean_train)
bean_val_processed = fitted.transform(bean_validation)

# PCA (the sklearn stopgap for the unbuilt StepPCA), estimated on TRAINING:
num_cols = [c for c in bean_val_processed.columns if c != "class"]
pca = PCA(n_components=4, random_state=1601)
pca.fit(fitted.transform(bean_train).select(num_cols))
```
## Report
```{python}
print("--- transformed validation head (zv -> normalize) ---")
print(bean_val_processed.head())

scores = pl.DataFrame(
    pca.transform(bean_val_processed.select(num_cols)),
    schema=[f"PC{i+1}" for i in range(4)],
).with_columns(bean_val_processed["class"])               # kept for coloring
print("\n--- validation-set PC scores (plot-ready) ---")
print(scores.head())

# ── Loadings + variance (what tidy(id = "pca") gives in R)

loadings = pl.DataFrame({"term": num_cols}).with_columns([
    pl.Series(f"PC{i+1}", pca.components_[i]) for i in range(4)
])
top = (loadings.unpivot(index="term", variable_name="component")
       .with_columns(pl.col("value").abs().alias("abs_value"))
       .sort(["component", "abs_value"], descending=[False, True])
       .group_by("component", maintain_order=True).head(5))
print("\n--- top 5 loadings per component ---")
print(top)

print("\n--- percent variance explained, PC1-PC4 ---")
print((pca.explained_variance_ratio_ * 100).round(2))
```
